note: Original editorial orientation notes written for NEXT MOVE from general public knowledge of Indore. No prices, no businesses, no contact details. Neighbourhoods change quickly: visit in person and confirm before you commit.

localities.name: Vijay Nagar
localities.goodFor: Professionals who want offices, cafes, malls and eateries close by.
localities.watchOut: Traffic on the main stretch at peak hours; rents are often higher near the main road than a few lanes inside.
ask: How far is the place from the main road and your office?

localities.name: Bhawarkuan
localities.goodFor: Students who want PGs, hostels, tiffin and study spaces within walking distance.
localities.watchOut: Crowded lanes and high demand around exam seasons; check noise levels at the time you will study.

localities.name: Palasia
localities.goodFor: People who want a central address with easy access to other parts of the city.
localities.watchOut: Central addresses tend to cost more; compare against nearby localities.
ask: What is included in the rent?

localities.name: Scheme 54
localities.vibe: Residential-commercial pocket next to Vijay Nagar
localities.goodFor: Those who want Vijay Nagar access in a slightly calmer setting.
localities.watchOut: Lanes vary a lot in feel; walk around in the evening before deciding.
ask: How long is the commute at your usual hour?

localities.name: Rajwada
localities.goodFor: Anyone who enjoys markets, street food and old-city character.
localities.watchOut: Narrow roads and heavy crowds, especially in the evening and on festival days.
ask: Is the lane reachable by an auto or a car?
How is the noise at night?

localities.name: Khajrana
localities.goodFor: Those looking for a lived-in neighbourhood with local shops close to home.
localities.watchOut: Congestion around the temple area on busy days.
ask: What do neighbours say about water and power cuts?

localities.name: Rajendra Nagar
localities.goodFor: People who prefer a calmer residential setting over a busy commercial one.
localities.watchOut: Check evening transport options if you work late.
ask: How do you get around after dark?

localities.name: Super Corridor
localities.goodFor: People whose office or college is in this belt and who want to avoid a long daily trip.
localities.watchOut: Fewer shops and eateries in some stretches; confirm what is within walking distance.
ask: Where is the nearest grocery and pharmacy?

localities.name: Rau
localities.vibe: Southern edge of the city, institutes nearby
localities.goodFor: Students and staff linked to institutions on the southern side.
localities.watchOut: Longer trips into the city centre; plan your regular route first.
ask: How will you reach the centre without your own vehicle?

localities.name: Mhow
localities.vibe: Separate cantonment town outside Indore proper
localities.goodFor: Those with a work or study link in Mhow itself.
localities.watchOut: It is a separate town; daily travel into Indore adds real time and cost.
ask: What is the realistic door-to-door commute?

firstWeek.title: Walk the lanes at two different times
firstWeek.text: Visit the place once in the daytime and once after dark. Noise, lighting and crowds change a lot.

firstWeek.title: Get terms in writing
firstWeek.text: Rent, deposit, notice period and what is included should be written down before you pay anything.

firstWeek.title: Test your real commute
firstWeek.text: Do the trip at the hour you will actually travel, not on a quiet Sunday.

firstWeek.title: Find the basics within 10 minutes
firstWeek.text: A grocery, a pharmacy and a place to eat that suits your diet make the first week far easier.

local.name: Sarafa Bazaar
local.what: Old-city market known for its evening street food.

local.name: 56 Dukan (Chhappan Dukan)
local.what: A well-known food street popular for snacks and sweets.

local.name: Rajwada Palace
local.what: The historic palace at the heart of the old city.

local.name: Lalbagh Palace
local.what: Former royal residence, a landmark on the city's southwest side.
